title: Unified Requests Facade adoption plan and phased shutdown of multipart-batch endpoints
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We introduced multipart-batch endpoints in 2023 to support large synchronous embedding and bulk-generate workflows. Over time the Unified Requests Facade (URF) has become the canonical surface for batching, streaming, and structured responses. This ticket defines the acceptance criteria, migration steps, telemetry gates, and communication plan to phase out multipart-batch endpoints with minimal client disruption.
motivation: Reduce surface area and maintenance cost, simplify routing and SLO guarantees, and shift clients to URF which supports more robust retries, structured outputs, and better telemetry for quality regression detection.
scope: In-scope: deprecate /v1/multipart-batch endpoints (embeddings-batch, generate-batch), publish SDK adapters for URF, add server-side compatibility logging and shadow routing for 12 weeks. Out-of-scope: on-prem private deployments (will schedule separate opt-in deprecation windows).
acceptance_criteria: Official deprecation notice published and emailed to all customers using multipart-batch endpoints with migration guides linked
SDK: adapters released in JS/Python/Rust that translate multipart-batch calls to URF preserving idempotency and throttling semantics
Telemetry: migration gate dashboard shows <5% error regression and <=10% increase in P95 latency for migrated traffic during shadow phase
Runtime: automated routing fallback to legacy endpoints during controlled traffic spikes for first 30 days post-shutdown
Docs: step-by-step migration guide, sample code for streaming and structured outputs, and compatibility matrix added to docs.redwood.com
Rollout: staged shutdown executed with canaries (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and rollback hooks; no customer-impact incidents classified as Sev2+ during rollout
tasks: Create and publish PRD (this ticket will reference the PRD and migration checklist)
Engineering: implement server-side shadow routing and enhanced telemetry for multipart-batch traffic
SDK: implement adapter helpers and a migration lint rule; publish beta packages
Docs: write migration guide, FAQ, and example app conversion tutorial
Support: draft customer email templates and runbook for common migration support requests
Comm: schedule webinar and Q&A office hours for top 40 paying customers using endpoints
Launch: run stepwise deprecation with telemetry gates and post-mortem template ready
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: undiscovered client edge-cases where multipart semantics differ from URF. Mitigation: keep legacy endpoints available as fallback for 90 days after shutdown initiation and offer dedicated eng support for affected customers.
Risk: latency regressions on URF for very large batch sizes. Mitigation: recommend and auto-suggest chunking profiles and enable prioritized routing to high-memory nodes for flagged customers.
Risk: SDK adoption lag. Mitigation: provide adapter CLI that rewrites client calls and CI lint checks to find uses of deprecated endpoints.
Risk: private/on-prem customers cannot accept remote changes. Mitigation: coordinate separate opt-in maintenance windows with SRE and Account teams.
communication_plan: T-minus 90d: public deprecation RFC and timeline published in console + status.redwood.com
T-minus 60d: targeted customer outreach (top paying customers and high-volume users)
T-minus 30d: SDK beta release; migration guide live; webinar announce
T-minus 14d: automated in-console notices and in-API deprecation warning headers
Shutdown week: hourly telemetry checks and comms channel staffed by eng+support
Post-shutdown 30d: follow-up email with migration coverage summary and opt-in extended support
telemetry_gates: Pre-canary: baseline dashboards capturing P50/P95 latency, 4xx/5xx rates, and token cost per request for multipart-batch traffic
Canary: move <=10% traffic to URF; require 0.5% or lower 5xx increase and P95 delta <=15% to proceed
Full rollout gate: aggregated error regression <=1% and customer-reported blockers <=2 across top 100 accounts
Rollback criteria: any sustained increase in Sev1/Sev2 incidents or missing SLO for >30 minutes
support_and_operational_playbooks: Support runbook with triage checklist and escalation path to eng on-call
Rollback playbook to re-enable legacy endpoints and route affected customers to fallback pool
Post-mortem template tied to the rollout to capture root cause and remediation steps
